sections.title: there is no perfect interface.
sections.body:
mobile, tablet, desktop were breakpoints. now the breakpoint is context: device, situation, attention, ability, whether the user is human at all. some want to talk to an app. some meet it inside another app. some need it glanceable, some need it deep.

and the agents we work with are learning to read the room: not just files and world state, but where we are, what we are doing, how much space we have. an interface is an expression that matches a context, and contexts have multiplied past what any single designed face can cover.

sections.title: an app is a spreadsheet wearing an experience.
sections.body:
apps have always been data with an experience layer on top. add functions to a spreadsheet and you have a program. we collect static files and call them second brains, but knowledge and language are never static.

so the file becomes a small durable state machine at a url: a little program that holds its data and can change it, living at one web address. every change lands one at a time, in order. it can be watched over a websocket and written by many hands. its id is tied to its host, so it carries provenance and identity. multiplayer by default, alive on its own.

sections.title: separate church from state.
sections.body:
the design is not the app. we call the designed side the church: screens, chats, voices, all replaceable. we call what remains the state: the data, plus the actions that may change it. those actions, we call verbs. smart contracts made the frontend optional, anyone can build one or interact directly. but their manuals live outside, in docs.

here the manual is baked in. ping the address and receive the charter: what it is, what it can do, how to speak to it. a stranger with nothing but the url has everything, and if the charter leaves a question open, that is a defect in the charter.

sections.title: nothing is hidden.
sections.body:
the verbs are code, and the code is stored as text you may read. the state is a document you may fetch. every amendment to the charter is kept in history. an app can be audited from the outside, in one request.

and the law is enforced, not promised. this app's allowedHosts list is empty, so its verbs cannot reach the network at all: pure functions of state, input, clock and seed.

sections.title: the intelligence stays outside.
sections.body:
the platform stores state and runs verbs. it decides nothing. every decision arrives from outside, carried by whoever visits: a person, a script, an agent.

keeping the intelligence outside, instead of building it into the center, is what makes many actors natural. many hands reading and writing the same small machines, closer to biology than to platforms. it is also why this page is shared.

and once a day the installation acts with nobody present. at midnight utc the look app's schedule invokes reset, and the site returns to light, indigo, soft: one change each day made by no one at all. the memory records it like any other.

sections.title: verbs become tools.
sections.body:
a page that speaks webmcp registers an app's public verbs as browser tools. your agent discovers them the moment you arrive. nothing was installed, no account exists, no sdk was needed.

and you watch the same live state your agent acts on. say what you want; the tools carry it; every open screen follows.

sections.title: one app, many lenses.
sections.body:
a creator ships interfaces; the user is not tied to them. we call them faces, because none of them is ever the app's own face: an app has none. use an app as the creator intended. use it through your agent, its verbs become your agent's tools. or hand the charter to an agent and have it derive a face just for you, on the spot.

the same schema serves everyone: the person who can only speak, the person who cannot see, the person who wants one number on a watch face. accessibility stops being a separate version. below, one app seen twice.

sections.title: vibe code a face of your own.
sections.body:
the derive door is the widest one. hand the charter to any agent and ask for the interface you want right now: a dashboard, a widget, one number for a watch face. the charter answers every question the agent will have.

faces built this way are yours and disposable. keep one for years or throw it away after a minute; the app does not notice either way.

sections.title: the design space opens.
sections.body:
none of this abolishes design; it multiplies the places where design happens. someone still shapes the chat's tone, the glanceable widget, the deep view. the work is no longer welded to one app.

and faces compose like lego: one face over many apps, built for a moment, thrown away after. tokens per second keep rising, and interfaces arrive just in time. this page is such a face, one lens over three apps.

sections.title: fork it.
sections.body: this site is its own white paper. three apps hold its words, its look, and its memory; the page you just read is one face over them. the proof is that it runs.
